name: Financial admin core vocabulary
description: The 100 terms a finance or accounts team member needs to know, from accounts assistant to head of finance.

cards.subject: ledger
says: is a record of the financial transactions for one account or category
gathers entries so that a balance can be worked out
cards.use: need to see all of the transactions for one account
not: is a summary statement of the whole company's profit

cards.subject: general ledger
says: holds all of an organisation's accounts in one record
is the source for the trial balance and the financial statements
cards.use: need the master record that all of the accounts feed into
not: records only the bills sent to customers

cards.subject: double-entry bookkeeping
says: records every transaction as equal debits and credits in at least two accounts
keeps the books in balance
cards.use: need a system where each transaction affects two sides
not: records each transaction once in a single list

cards.subject: debit
says: is an entry on the left side of an account
increases assets and expenses
cards.use: need to record an increase in an asset such as the bank balance
not: is an entry on the right side that increases income

cards.subject: credit
says: is an entry on the right side of an account
increases liabilities and income
cards.use: need to record that income has been earned
not: is an entry on the left side that increases assets

cards.subject: journal entry
says: records a transaction or adjustment by listing its debits and credits
normally carries a date, a reference and a description
cards.use: need to correct a posting or record a transaction that has no invoice
not: is a daily diary of what the finance team did

cards.subject: chart of accounts
says: is the numbered list of accounts used to categorise every transaction
sets how income and costs are grouped in reports
cards.use: need to decide where a new type of cost should be recorded
not: is a graph of the company's monthly sales

cards.subject: trial balance
says: lists every ledger balance to check that the debits equal the credits
is the starting point for preparing the financial statements
cards.use: need to check that the books balance before preparing reports
not: is the final statement of the business's assets and liabilities

cards.subject: petty cash
says: is a small amount of physical cash kept for minor expenses
is topped up against receipts and counted regularly
cards.use: need to buy a small item on the spot with cash
not: is the main bank account of the business

cards.subject: source document
says: is the original evidence of a transaction, such as an invoice or receipt
supports each entry in the books
cards.use: need evidence for an entry in the books
not: is a summary report produced at month end

cards.subject: accounts receivable
says: is money that customers owe the business for goods or services already supplied
is an asset on the balance sheet
cards.use: need to know who still owes you money
not: is money the business owes to its suppliers

cards.subject: accounts payable
says: is money the business owes to suppliers for goods or services already received
is a liability on the balance sheet
cards.use: need to know what you still owe to suppliers
not: is money that customers owe the business

cards.subject: credit note
says: reduces the amount a customer owes by cancelling part or all of an invoice
is issued for returns, errors or discounts
cards.use: need to correct an invoice that was too high without deleting it
not: is a demand for payment sent after the due date

cards.subject: remittance advice
says: tells a supplier which invoices a payment covers
helps match a payment to the right invoices
cards.use: need to tell a supplier what a payment is for
not: cancels part of an invoice

cards.subject: aged debtors report
says: lists customer balances by how long they have been unpaid
shows which debts are most overdue
cards.use: need to see which customers are paying late
not: lists what the business owes to suppliers, grouped by age

cards.subject: credit period
says: is the number of days a customer has to pay an invoice
is stated on the invoice, for example 30 days
cards.use: need to say when an invoice is due
not: is the maximum amount a customer may owe

cards.subject: three-way match
says: compares the purchase order, the goods received note and the supplier invoice
stops payment for goods that were never ordered or received
cards.use: need to confirm that an invoice is for goods that were ordered and delivered
not: compares three months of bank statements

cards.subject: direct debit
says: lets a supplier collect varying amounts from your bank account with your authority
is protected by a guarantee if a payment is taken in error
cards.use: need to collect regular payments that may change in amount
not: is a fixed payment that you set up yourself for the same amount

cards.subject: standing order
says: is an instruction you give your bank to pay a fixed amount at set intervals
is set up and controlled by the payer
cards.use: need to pay the same rent on the same date each month
not: is a collection that the payee controls, with an amount that can vary

cards.subject: bad debt
says: is an amount owed that is unlikely ever to be paid
is written off as an expense
cards.use: find that a customer has gone out of business owing you money
not: is a debt that is paid early

cards.subject: bank reconciliation
says: compares the cash book with the bank statement to find differences
explains timing differences and errors
cards.use: need to check that the books agree with the bank
not: compares the trial balance with the balance sheet

cards.subject: bank statement
says: is the bank's record of money in and out of an account
is the evidence used in a bank reconciliation
cards.use: need proof of what has gone through the bank
not: is the company's own record of its cash transactions

cards.subject: cash book
says: is the company's own record of money paid into and out of the bank
is compared with the bank statement
cards.use: need the company's own record of bank transactions
not: is the bank's record of an account

cards.subject: cash flow
says: is the movement of money into and out of a business over a period
can be negative even when a business is profitable
cards.use: need to know whether there is enough cash to pay the bills
not: is the profit shown in the profit and loss account

cards.subject: cash flow forecast
says: predicts the cash coming in and going out over coming weeks or months
warns of future shortages
cards.use: need to see whether you can pay next month's bills
not: records last month's bank transactions

cards.subject: working capital
says: is current assets minus current liabilities
shows whether a business can meet its short-term obligations
cards.use: need to judge whether short-term assets cover short-term debts
not: is the cash held in the petty cash tin

cards.subject: overdraft
says: lets an account go below zero up to an agreed limit
charges interest or fees on the amount used
cards.use: need short-term borrowing on a bank account
not: is a fixed loan that is repaid in equal instalments

cards.subject: clearing
says: is the process that completes a payment so that the money can be used
takes longer for cheques than for electronic transfers
cards.use: find that a deposited payment is not yet available to spend
not: is the monthly check of the bank statement

cards.subject: Faster Payments
says: is the UK service for near-instant bank transfers
is used for most online and mobile payments
cards.use: need to send a payment that arrives in minutes
not: is the service for large payments that arrive only the same day

cards.subject: CHAPS
says: is the UK system for same-day high-value payments
is typically used for house purchases and large transfers
cards.use: need to send a very large payment that must arrive the same day
not: is the service for near-instant everyday transfers

cards.subject: VAT
says: is a tax charged on most goods and services at each stage of supply
is collected by businesses and paid over to HMRC
cards.use: need to add tax to a sale
not: is a tax on a company's profits

cards.subject: input VAT
says: is the VAT a business pays on its purchases
can usually be reclaimed from HMRC
cards.use: need to reclaim VAT that was paid on a supplier's invoice
not: is the VAT charged on a business's sales

cards.subject: output VAT
says: is the VAT a business charges on its sales
is paid over to HMRC after input VAT is deducted
cards.use: need to work out the VAT owed on sales
not: is the VAT paid on purchases and then reclaimed

cards.subject: PAYE
says: is the system for deducting income tax and National Insurance from pay
requires the employer to pay the deductions to HMRC
cards.use: need to deduct tax from employees' wages
not: is the tax a company pays on its profits

cards.subject: National Insurance
says: is a contribution taken from pay that builds entitlement to some state benefits
is deducted from employees and also paid by employers
cards.use: need to explain the other deduction on a payslip besides income tax
not: is a tax charged on the sale of goods

cards.subject: payslip
says: shows an employee's pay and deductions for a pay period
must be provided to each employee
cards.use: need to show an employee how their pay was worked out
not: is the yearly summary of pay and tax

cards.subject: P45
says: is given to an employee who leaves a job
shows pay and tax up to the leaving date
cards.use: need to give a leaver their pay and tax details
not: is the year-end summary given to people who stay

cards.subject: P60
says: is the end-of-year summary of an employee's pay and tax
is given to employees who are still working for the employer at the year end
cards.use: need to give staff their yearly pay and tax summary
not: is given only to people who leave

cards.subject: auto-enrolment
says: requires employers to enrol eligible workers in a workplace pension
lets workers opt out but does not let them be refused entry
cards.use: need to put eligible employees into a pension scheme
not: is a tax relief claimed on equipment

cards.subject: corporation tax
says: is a tax on a company's profits
is separate from VAT and from PAYE
cards.use: need to work out the tax owed on a company's profits
not: is deducted from each employee's wages

cards.subject: balance sheet
says: shows what a business owns, owes and is worth at one date
lists assets, liabilities and equity
cards.use: need to see the business's financial position on a given day
not: shows income and costs over a period

cards.subject: profit and loss account
says: shows income and costs over a period to give a profit or loss
is also called an income statement
cards.use: need to see whether the business made a profit last year
not: shows what the business owns and owes at one date

cards.subject: cash flow statement
says: shows how cash moved through operating, investing and financing activities
explains the change in cash over a period
cards.use: need to explain why cash fell even though profit rose
not: lists what the business owns and owes at one date

cards.subject: asset
says: is something a business owns that has value
includes cash, stock, equipment and money owed by customers
cards.use: need to name what a business owns
not: is something the business owes to others

cards.subject: liability
says: is something a business owes to others
includes loans, supplier bills and tax due
cards.use: need to name what a business owes
not: is something the business owns

cards.subject: equity
says: is what is left for the owners after liabilities are taken from assets
includes share capital and retained profit
cards.use: need to know the owners' stake in the business
not: is money the business owes to lenders

cards.subject: gross profit
says: is sales minus the direct cost of making or buying what was sold
is found before overheads are deducted
cards.use: need to see profit before running costs
not: is profit after all costs and tax

cards.subject: net profit
says: is what remains after all costs and tax are taken from income
is the bottom line of the profit and loss account
cards.use: need the final profit after all costs
not: is sales minus only the direct costs

cards.subject: depreciation
says: spreads the cost of a long-lived asset over its useful life
is a non-cash expense in the profit and loss account
cards.use: need to charge the cost of equipment over the years that it is used
not: is the amount a customer fails to pay

cards.subject: retained profit
says: is profit kept in the business rather than paid out to owners
builds up in equity from year to year
cards.use: need to show how much profit has been kept in the business
not: is the cash held in the bank at year end

cards.subject: accrual
says: records a cost or income in the period it relates to before the invoice or payment
is an estimate of something earned or incurred but not yet billed
cards.use: need to record a cost that belongs to this month but has not been invoiced
not: records a payment made in advance for a future period

cards.subject: prepayment
says: is a payment made in advance for something to be received in a future period
is held as an asset until it is used
cards.use: need to spread an annual insurance premium over the year
not: is a cost incurred but not yet invoiced

cards.subject: deferred income
says: is money received in advance for work not yet done
is held as a liability until the work is delivered
cards.use: have been paid for a year's subscription up front
not: is money owed by a customer for work already done

cards.subject: provision
says: is an amount set aside for a probable future cost of uncertain amount or timing
is recognised as a liability
cards.use: need to set aside money for a likely future claim
not: is a cost that has already been paid

cards.subject: month-end close
says: is the routine of finishing all entries and checks for a month
ends with reconciled accounts and a set of reports
cards.use: need to finish and lock the accounts for the month
not: is the yearly shutdown of the whole business

cards.subject: year-end close
says: finalises the accounts for the financial year
includes adjustments, stock counts and preparing the statutory accounts
cards.use: need to prepare the books for the annual accounts and audit
not: is a short routine that is done every month

cards.subject: accounting period
says: is the length of time covered by a set of accounts
can be a month, a quarter or a year
cards.use: need to know which period a transaction belongs to
not: is the date by which a tax return is due

cards.subject: suspense account
says: is a temporary account that holds amounts until their proper place is known
should be cleared to zero before reporting
cards.use: find a bank receipt that you cannot yet identify
not: is a permanent account for staff loans

cards.subject: write-off
says: removes a balance from the books because it will not be recovered
is recorded as an expense
cards.use: decide that an old customer debt will never be paid
not: is a payment that is made in advance

cards.subject: reversing journal
says: cancels an earlier journal automatically at the start of the next period
is often used for accruals
cards.use: need an accrual to drop out automatically next month
not: corrects an entry that was posted to the wrong supplier

cards.subject: cost centre
says: is a part of an organisation to which costs are assigned
has no income of its own in the accounts
cards.use: need to see how much a department spends
not: is a part of the business that is judged on its profit

cards.subject: budget variance
says: is the difference between a budgeted figure and the actual result
can be favourable or adverse
cards.use: see that spending is above the plan
not: is the total amount set aside for the year

cards.subject: rolling forecast
says: is updated regularly and always looks a fixed period ahead
adds a new period as each period ends
cards.use: want a forecast that always covers the next twelve months
not: is a budget that is fixed once for the year and never updated

cards.subject: zero-based budgeting
says: builds each budget from zero, requiring every cost to be justified
does not assume last year's spending carries over
cards.use: need every cost to be justified instead of rolling last year's budget forward
not: sets next year's budget as last year's plus a percentage

cards.subject: break-even point
says: is the level of sales at which total revenue equals total costs
is where a business makes neither profit nor loss
cards.use: need to know how much to sell to cover all costs
not: is the date by which a loan is repaid

cards.subject: gross margin
says: is gross profit shown as a percentage of sales
shows how much of each pound of sales remains after direct costs
cards.use: need to compare profitability on sales across products
not: is the profit after tax

cards.subject: overhead cost
says: is a running cost that is not tied to a particular product or sale
includes rent, utilities and administration salaries
cards.use: need to name a cost that is not tied to one product
not: is the cost of materials in a product

cards.subject: management reporting
says: gives managers internal financial information to make decisions
can be produced monthly in a format that need not follow statutory rules
cards.use: need internal numbers to make decisions during the year
not: is the set of accounts filed publicly each year

cards.subject: fixed cost
says: stays the same however much is produced or sold in the period
includes rent and salaries
cards.use: need to identify costs that do not change with sales
not: rises each time another unit is sold

cards.subject: variable cost
says: changes with the amount produced or sold
includes materials and sales commission
cards.use: need to identify costs that rise with sales
not: stays the same however much is sold

cards.subject: internal control
says: is a procedure that protects assets, prevents errors and reduces fraud
includes approvals, reconciliations and access limits
cards.use: need safeguards that stop errors and fraud in the finance process
not: is an outside firm's review of the accounts

cards.subject: segregation of duties
says: splits key tasks between people so that one person cannot complete a risky process alone
stops the same person raising and approving a payment
cards.use: need to ensure the person paying a supplier is not the person who approved it
not: gives one person control over every step

cards.subject: authorisation limit
says: is the maximum amount a person may approve
sends larger amounts to someone more senior
cards.use: need to decide who can approve a large payment
not: is the maximum amount a customer may owe

cards.subject: audit trail
says: is the record that shows who did what and when to a transaction
lets a figure be traced back to its source
cards.use: need to trace a figure back to the original document
not: is a yearly summary of the audit's findings

cards.subject: external audit
says: is an independent examination of the financial statements by an outside firm
gives an opinion on whether they give a true and fair view
cards.use: need an independent opinion on the annual accounts
not: is a check carried out by the company's own staff

cards.subject: internal audit
says: is a review of controls and processes carried out by the organisation's own team
reports to management and the board
cards.use: need an in-house check on whether controls work
not: gives an opinion on the published financial statements

cards.subject: materiality
says: is the size at which an error or omission could affect a reader's decisions
helps decide how much effort to spend on small differences
cards.use: need to decide whether a small difference is worth correcting or investigating
not: is the cost of the materials used in making a product

cards.subject: going concern
says: is the assumption that a business will continue operating for the foreseeable future
is assessed by directors and checked by auditors
cards.use: need to assess whether a business can keep trading for the next twelve months
not: is a business that is about to be sold

cards.subject: management letter
says: is a letter from auditors to management setting out control weaknesses and recommendations
is issued after an audit
cards.use: receive the auditors' recommendations for improving controls
not: is an invitation to a management meeting

cards.subject: anti-money laundering
says: is the set of rules and checks that stop criminal money being disguised as legitimate
requires checks on customers and reporting of suspicion
cards.use: need to check who a customer really is before taking their money
not: is a tax on large cash payments

cards.subject: bank feed
says: imports bank transactions into accounting software automatically
saves typing and speeds up reconciliation
cards.use: want bank transactions to appear in the books without typing
not: sends payments to suppliers in a batch

cards.subject: payment run
says: pays a batch of approved supplier invoices at one time
is approved before the payments are sent to the bank
cards.use: need to pay all of the invoices that are due this week
not: imports bank transactions into the books

cards.subject: approval workflow
says: routes a document such as an invoice to the right people to approve
records who approved it and when
cards.use: need invoices to be approved by the right person before payment
not: is a report of overdue invoices

cards.subject: expense policy
says: sets out what staff may claim and how
sets limits and the evidence required
cards.use: need to know whether a cost can be claimed
not: lists the amounts approved for each department's budget

cards.subject: record retention
says: sets how long financial records must be kept
is set by law and company policy
cards.use: need to know how long to keep invoices and receipts
not: is the process of copying records to a backup

cards.subject: Making Tax Digital
says: requires certain tax records to be kept digitally and returns to be sent through compatible software
is a UK programme run by HMRC
cards.use: need to submit VAT returns through compatible software
not: is a scheme that removes the need to pay tax

cards.subject: Companies House
says: is the UK register of companies where accounts and filings are lodged
holds public information about company directors and accounts
cards.use: need to file annual accounts for a UK company
not: is the tax authority that collects VAT

cards.subject: statutory reporting
says: prepares the annual accounts a company must produce and file by law
follows accounting standards and a set deadline
cards.use: need to prepare the annual accounts that the law requires
not: gives managers internal figures during the year

cards.subject: accounting standard
says: is a rulebook for how transactions must be recorded and reported
makes accounts comparable between organisations
cards.use: need to know how a transaction must be recognised in the accounts
not: is a limit on how much a person may approve

cards.subject: HMRC
says: is the UK tax authority
collects taxes such as VAT, PAYE and corporation tax
cards.use: need to know who collects the taxes
not: is the register where companies file their accounts

cards.subject: liquidity
says: is how easily a business can meet its short-term payments
depends on how much cash it holds or can reach quickly
cards.use: need to judge whether the business can pay its short-term bills
not: is the total value of everything the business owns

cards.subject: gearing
says: is the proportion of a business's funding that comes from debt
rises when borrowing grows compared with equity
cards.use: need to see how heavily the business relies on borrowing
not: is how quickly a business converts stock to cash

cards.subject: EBITDA
says: is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation
is often used as a rough indicator of operating performance
cards.use: need a measure of operating profit before financing and non-cash charges
not: is the cash left after all payments

cards.subject: covenant
says: is a condition in a loan agreement that the borrower must keep to
can allow the lender to demand repayment if broken
cards.use: need to check what conditions a lender has set on a loan
not: is a tax relief on interest

cards.subject: hedging
says: reduces exposure to a risk such as exchange-rate or interest-rate movements
uses contracts that offset a possible loss
cards.use: need to protect against a currency moving against you
not: increases exposure to a risk to try to earn more

cards.subject: cost of capital
says: is the return an organisation must earn to satisfy those who fund it
is used as the hurdle rate for investments
cards.use: need the minimum return that a new project must beat
not: is the price of buying a capital asset

cards.subject: investor reporting
says: gives investors regular information about performance, cash and risks
is usually agreed in the investment terms
cards.use: need to send investors a regular update on performance
not: files the annual accounts at the public register

cards.subject: financial model
says: is a spreadsheet or tool that projects financial results from stated assumptions
is used to test different scenarios
cards.use: need to test what a decision would do to profit and cash
not: is a record of past transactions

cards.subject: scenario analysis
says: tests how results change under different assumptions
often looks at best, base and worst cases
cards.use: need to know how results would change if sales fell
not: is the check of one invoice against an order

cards.subject: treasury policy
says: sets how an organisation manages cash, borrowing, investments and financial risk
sets limits on counterparties and exposure
cards.use: need rules for how surplus cash may be invested
not: sets the rules for which staff expenses can be claimed

qa.q: Which statement shows what a business owns and owes at a particular date?
qa.why: The balance sheet is a snapshot of assets, liabilities and equity.

qa.q: Which of these is a liability?
qa.why: A liability is something the business owes.

qa.q: Who collects VAT?
qa.why: HMRC is the UK tax authority.

qa.q: What shows an employee how their pay was worked out?
qa.why: A payslip shows pay and deductions for a pay period.

qa.q: What evidence supports an entry for a purchase from a supplier?
qa.why: An invoice is a source document.

qa.q: You are unsure whether a taxi fare can be claimed. Where do you look first?
qa.why: The expense policy says what may be claimed.

qa.q: A customer pays you 1,000 into the bank. What is the entry in the bank account?
qa.why: Receiving money increases an asset, which is a debit.

qa.q: A customer owes you money for work already done. What is this called?
qa.why: Money owed to you by customers is a receivable.

qa.q: A customer returns goods that were already invoiced. What do you issue?
qa.why: A credit note reduces what the customer owes.

qa.q: A gym takes a monthly amount that can change from your account under your authority. What is it?
qa.why: A payee collects the amount under a direct debit.

qa.q: You pay the same rent on the same date each month by instruction to your bank. What is it?
qa.why: A standing order is a fixed instruction set up by the payer.

qa.q: Which statement tells you whether the business made a profit last year?
qa.why: The profit and loss account shows income and costs over a period.

qa.q: Sales are 100,000, direct costs are 60,000 and overheads are 30,000. What is the gross profit?
qa.why: Gross profit is sales minus direct costs.

qa.q: Rent is the same however much is sold. What type of cost is it?
qa.why: A fixed cost does not change with sales.

qa.q: The books show 5,000 in the bank but the bank statement shows 4,200. Which task finds out why?
qa.why: A reconciliation compares the books with the bank.

qa.q: A profitable business runs out of cash. What is a likely reason?
qa.right: Customers have not yet paid, so the profit is not yet cash
wrong: The chart of accounts is too long
qa.why: Profit and cash flow can differ because of timing.

qa.q: You need to deduct income tax and National Insurance from employees' wages. Which system do you use?
qa.why: PAYE is the system for deductions from pay.

qa.q: Electricity was used in March but the invoice arrives in April. How should March record it?
qa.why: An accrual records a cost in the period it relates to.

qa.q: A year's insurance was paid in January. How is it treated in the monthly accounts?
qa.right: Held as a prepayment and charged a twelfth each month
qa.why: A prepayment is spread over the period it covers.

qa.q: Which report shows which customers are paying late?
qa.why: The aged debtors report lists balances by age.

qa.q: A van costs 20,000 and is expected to last five years. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the yearly charge?
qa.why: 20,000 divided by five years is 4,000.

qa.q: Fixed costs are 10,000 and each unit sold contributes 5 towards them. How many units must be sold to break even?
qa.why: 10,000 divided by 5 is 2,000.

qa.q: Actual spending is 12,000 against a budget of 10,000. What is the variance?
qa.why: Spending above the budget is an adverse variance.

qa.q: Debits total 120,000 and credits total 118,500 in the trial balance. What does this show?
qa.right: There is an error somewhere in the books
qa.why: Debits must equal credits.

qa.q: One clerk raises, approves and pays the same supplier invoice. What control is weak?
qa.why: No one person should do a risky process alone.

qa.q: A cost was posted to the wrong account. What do you use to correct it?
qa.why: A journal moves a posting between accounts.

qa.q: What does a P60 show?
qa.right: An employee's pay and tax for the year, given to those still working for the employer
wrong: Pay and tax up to leaving, for leavers
qa.why: A P60 is the year-end summary.

qa.q: You paid VAT on a supplier's invoice. What is it called, and what usually happens to it?
qa.right: Input VAT, which can usually be reclaimed
wrong: Output VAT, which is paid to the supplier
Corporation tax, which is paid at year end
Gross profit, which is carried forward
qa.why: Input VAT is VAT on purchases.

qa.q: An old customer debt will never be paid. What do you do?
qa.right: Write it off as an expense
wrong: Put it in the cash book
qa.why: Unrecoverable debts are written off.

qa.q: Assets are 500,000 and liabilities are 300,000. What is the equity?
qa.why: Equity is assets minus liabilities.

qa.q: A buyer must send a house deposit that has to arrive the same day. Which payment method fits?
qa.why: CHAPS is for same-day high-value payments.

qa.q: An invoice arrives for goods nobody remembers ordering. Which control would catch this?
qa.why: A three-way match compares order, delivery note and invoice.

qa.q: A customer pays a year's subscription in advance. How is it treated?
qa.right: As deferred income, released month by month
wrong: As revenue in full on receipt
qa.why: Money for work not yet done is a liability.

qa.q: An unknown receipt of 500 appears in the bank. Where is it held until identified?
qa.why: A suspense account holds items until they are identified.

qa.q: Current assets are 80,000 and current liabilities are 100,000. What does this suggest?
qa.right: The business may find it hard to meet short-term obligations
qa.why: Working capital is negative.

qa.q: Which review gives an independent opinion on the published annual accounts?
qa.why: External auditors give an independent opinion.

qa.q: A new customer offers a large cash payment and is vague about where the money comes from. What should you do?
qa.right: Follow anti-money-laundering procedures and report your suspicion through the proper channel
wrong: Accept the cash to keep the customer
Ask them to split it into smaller payments
Tell the customer you plan to report them
qa.why: Suspicion must be reported through the proper channel without tipping off.

qa.q: You want a forecast that always covers the next twelve months. Which approach fits?
qa.why: A rolling forecast adds a period as each ends.

qa.q: Profit rose but cash fell, and the board wants to know why. Which statement explains it?
qa.why: The cash flow statement explains the change in cash.

qa.q: Staff turn 22 and are eligible for a workplace pension. What must the employer do?
qa.right: Enrol them under auto-enrolment, letting them opt out if they wish
wrong: Refuse entry if they earn too little
qa.why: Employers must enrol eligible workers.

qa.q: You need to set aside money for a likely future legal claim of uncertain amount. What do you record?
wrong: An accrual for a received invoice
qa.why: A provision is for a probable cost of uncertain amount or timing.

qa.q: You are deciding whether a small difference of a few pounds is worth investigating. Which concept applies?
qa.why: Materiality is the size that could affect a reader's decisions.

qa.q: The directors are unsure whether the business can keep trading for the next twelve months. Which assumption is in question?
qa.why: Going concern is assumed to continue for the foreseeable future.

qa.q: You want an accrual to drop out of the books automatically next month. What do you use?
qa.why: A reversing journal cancels an earlier journal automatically.

qa.q: A borrower's ratio falls below the level in the loan agreement. What may the lender do?
qa.right: Demand repayment or renegotiate the terms
qa.why: A broken covenant can trigger the lender's rights.

qa.q: A company sells in dollars but reports in pounds and wants to protect against a falling dollar. What does it use?
qa.why: Hedging offsets exchange-rate risk.

qa.q: Auditors send management a letter listing weaknesses in controls. What is it called?
qa.why: A management letter sets out weaknesses and recommendations.

qa.q: The CFO wants to know how profit and cash would change if sales fell by 20 per cent. What does she run?
qa.right: Scenario analysis using the financial model
qa.why: Scenario analysis tests different assumptions.

qa.q: A new project is expected to return less than what funders require. What should the board compare it against?
qa.why: The cost of capital is the hurdle rate.

qa.q: Two companies use different rules for recording the same transaction. Which framework makes accounts comparable?
qa.why: Accounting standards set how transactions are recorded.
